I am 32 years old and I only finished primary school, so I don't read many books about farming. But I have been helping my family in the fields since I was a child, and now I manage our land while my husband works in a factory in the city. We have about 8 mu of good flat land in Quzhou, and I always grow winter wheat and summer maize on all of it. This is what everyone in our village does, the grain station buys wheat at a guaranteed price, and I know how to manage these crops with my own hands. 

For wheat, I will buy improved seeds from the township store — last year I used Jimai and it yielded well, so I will do the same. I use the rotary tiller before sowing in October. I put down compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea in spring when the wheat turns green. I irrigate three times: once before winter, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I also spray pesticides about four times to control aphids and weeds. After harvesting wheat in early June, I immediately plant maize. I use Denghai hybrid seeds because they grow fast and yield high. For maize, I don't till much — I drill the seeds directly into the wheat stubble to save time and diesel. I apply some compound fertilizer at planting and urea at the big trumpet stage, and irrigate twice because summer rains usually help. I spray pesticides about four times for maize borers and weeds. I don't grow cotton anymore because it needs too many sprays and my back hurts from picking it. I keep some grain for our own flour and cornmeal, and sell the rest to traders who come to the village.
